slides.heading: Knuth Morris Pratt Algorithm
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Knuth Morris Pratt Algorithm, a very hard famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Does sub occur in str? Prefix-function (failure table) matching.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A failure table tells us how far to fall back on a mismatch, so we never rescan the text.
slides.narration: A failure table tells us how far to fall back on a mismatch, so we never rescan the text.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Naive matching can rescan the same text many times. KMP's failure table lets the text pointer only move forward, linear overall.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Build the prefix function of the pattern
3. On mismatch, fall back via the table
4. Match when the pattern is complete
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build the prefix function of the pattern. Second, walk the text. Third, on mismatch, fall back via the table. Fourth, match when the pattern is complete.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Build the failure table
slides.narration: The failure table stores, for each prefix, the longest proper prefix that's also a suffix.

slides.narration: Scanning the text, a mismatch doesn't restart from scratch; we fall back to the failure value and keep going.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Match found
slides.narration: When the matched length reaches the pattern's length, we've found it.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We build fail with a k pointer that falls back on mismatches. Then we scan the text with the same logic, returning true when k equals the pattern length.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n plus m. Space is O of m.

bullets: Build fail with the same loop
